h: From giant bouncy castles to the clockwork orange
p: Inflatable obstacle courses look easy until you're three sections in and your legs have turned to jelly. The trick is to treat it like a series of short races rather than one long marathon: have a go, have a breather, then go again. Younger children will want to explore the softer areas at their own pace, while older ones will be challenging you to rematch after rematch. Pack a water bottle and get there early enough to sort shoes and coats before your slot starts.

Once you're done, Glasgow has loads to add on. The Glasgow Science Centre on the south bank of the Clyde has hands-on exhibits, a planetarium and the striking tower beside it, and it's ideal for curious kids. Over on Glasgow Green, the People's Palace tells the story of everyday Glaswegian life and has the Winter Gardens glasshouse alongside.

For something outdoors, Pollok Country Park is home to a herd of shaggy Highland cattle and the Burrell Collection, which reopened after a big refurbishment and is free to visit. Glasgow Cathedral and the Necropolis on the hill behind it make for an atmospheric wander with great city views. Getting around is part of the fun too: the Glasgow Subway, a little circular line nicknamed the Clockwork Orange, loops around the city centre and West End, and kids love its tiny orange trains. Day passes make it easy to hop between the West End, the city centre and the south side, so you can squeeze a couple of free museums in around your bounce without ever touching the car.
